| Leg | Approx. Driving Distance |

| **Rivermist → San Francisco** | ≈ 250–350 mi (≈ 400–560 km) |

> *Why the range?*  
> – “Rivermist” isn’t a standard ZIP‑code reference, so the mileage depends on its actual latitude/longitude. For most places named Rivermist in northern California (e.g., near Redding or Yuba City), the fastest routes run roughly 260–320 miles along US‑97 → US‑395 → CA‑99 → I‑80 → SF. If it’s further north (close to the Oregon border), expect closer to 330–360 miles.*

### Fuel Planning Checklist

| Item | Recommendation |
|------|---------------|
| **Average MPG** | Check your owner’s manual—most midsize cars hit 24–30 mpg combined. |
| **Fuel Tank Capacity** | Typical tanks hold 12–16 gal. With 28 mpg, that gives 336–448 mi of range. |
| **Stop Points** | Plan a mid‑trip stop (around halfway) for gas & stretch—ideally near a rest area or service station on I‑80 or CA‑49. |
| **Extra Gas** | Keep a spare 2–3 gal in the trunk if possible—it adds another 60–90 mi of safety margin. |
| **Weather / Traffic** | Heavy traffic or mountain passes can drop your mpg by 10–20%. Factor that into your calculations. |

Assume:
- Vehicle avg. 26 mpg
- Full tank 14 gal → 364 mi range

If your leg is 310 mi, you’ll finish with ~54 % tank left. That’s plenty for a short detour or a quick pitstop. If the leg turns out to be 340 mi, you’re still within safe limits but consider topping off after the midway break.

---

**Bottom line:** A direct drive from Rivermist to San Francisco will take roughly 4½–5 hours under normal conditions and covers about 280–350 miles. Your usual sedan should comfortably make the trip without needing a full refill en‑route—but double‑check your exact starting point and local traffic patterns to fine‑tune the numbers. Safe travels!
